explanation: The Almighty Creator who is the object of Paul's devotion and the source of righteousness through faith in Christ.
Jesus, the Son of God, who became incarnate, died, and rose again to give people salvation and new life in him.
In this chapter, it does not refer to one's own morality or law-abiding behavior, but to the righteousness received from God through faith in Christ.
The Jewish legislation given by Moses; Paul argues that adherence to this alone cannot bring salvation.
The detailed religious rules and ritual requirements belonging to the old covenant, which Paul regards as loss compared to Christ.
Paul's description of how everything he once considered gain (status, religion) is now seen as lost or worthless in order to win Christ.
What one obtains by casting aside all other things; it is the very person of Jesus and life in him that becomes the true gain.
The deep, personal experience of Christ that Paul places above all other knowledge or religious achievement.
In the context of Philippians 3, this refers both to Jesus' resurrection and the hope that believers will also be transformed to resemble him in their own future resurrection.
The sufferings Paul endures for the sake of Christ, which he regards as an honor and a sign of true devotion.
